`Signer.sign` uses the signer's key alone; `Signer.unsign` tries the key and then each fallback in turn, and `PasswordResetTokenGenerator.check_token` does the same with its secrets (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.unsign`, `django/contrib/auth/tokens.py:PasswordResetTokenGenerator.check_token`).

`Signer.sign` uses the signer's key alone; `Signer.unsign` tries the key and then each fallback in turn, and `PasswordResetTokenGenerator.check_token` does the same with its secrets (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.unsign`, `django/contrib/auth/tokens.py:PasswordResetTokenGenerator.check_token`).

The documentation's way of rotating a key follows: the new key in `SECRET_KEY`, the old one at the front of `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS`, removed when what was made with it may expire (`docs/ref/settings.txt`).

A session's data stored in the database or a file that does not verify is logged to `"django.security.SuspiciousSession"` and read as an empty session (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.decode`).

A user whose session hash was made under neither the key nor a fallback has the session flushed and is anonymous; one whose hash was made under a fallback keeps the session, under a new session key, with the hash made again under the new key (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:get_user`).
Passwords are hashed with salts of their own, and the documentation says a change of key does not affect them (`docs/ref/settings.txt`).
Salt, secret and value may each be a string or bytes: `force_bytes` makes them bytes (`django/utils/crypto.py:salted_hmac`).
Since 6.1 a call that names no algorithm warns with `RemovedInDjango2028Warning`, and in Django 2028 the default becomes `"sha256"` (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
`constant_time_compare` makes both values bytes and returns what `secrets.compare_digest` says of them (`django/utils/crypto.py:constant_time_compare`).

`get_random_string` makes a string of the length asked for, each character chosen by `secrets.choice` from the characters it is given: `RANDOM_STRING_CHARS`, the letters of both cases and the digits, unless it is given others (`django/utils/crypto.py:get_random_string`).

Among its users are the CSRF secret, 32 letters and digits; a session's key, 32 of `VALID_KEY_CHARS`, lower-case letters and digits; the salts of the password hashers but the bcrypt ones (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:BasePasswordHasher.salt`); and a new project's key.
`pbkdf2` is `hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac` with SHA-256 unless another digest is given, and a derived key as long as the digest's output unless a length is given (`django/utils/crypto.py:pbkdf2`).

The startproject command ([The commands Django ships](../commands/builtin.md)) writes into the new project's settings a key of `"django-insecure-"` followed by 50 characters from `get_random_secret_key`, drawn by `get_random_string` from lower-case letters, digits and punctuation (`django/core/management/commands/startproject.py:Command.handle`, `django/core/management/utils.py:get_random_secret_key`).
